title: Collective collapse of label-free majority-vote RL
setting: N binary problems, each with a hidden true answer, share one parameter v through logits z_i = u_i + lam*v. The initial lean is correct for 65% of problems, and leans are balanced across the two answers. The learner is trained for a fixed 2500 steps of minibatch REINFORCE on the K=3 majority-vote self-reward, with no labels. The metric is the expected accuracy on the problems' hidden true answers under fresh samples; labels are never used in training.

paper.title: Collective Dynamics of Self-Reinforcement: How Cross-Task Coupling Drives Policy Collapse in Unsupervised RLVR
paper.claim: Collapse of self-rewarded training onto one answer appears only when the number of problems exceeds a critical size that shrinks as the shared coupling grows, and it vanishes when the shared direction is removed or when the initial model is confident.

metric.name: accuracy
metric.description: Expected probability of the true answer (averaged over problems) under the final policy, i.e. accuracy on fresh samples. Sharpening alone lifts it to about the 0.65 initial-majority accuracy. Collapse to a single answer drives it toward 0.5.

factors.name: method
factors.description: plain: majority-vote self-training with the shared direction active. no_shared: the shared direction is removed (lam=0), so each problem trains independently. entropy_bonus: plain training plus a batch-level marginal-entropy bonus (weight 0.75) that damps the uniform shared mode.

factors.name: N
factors.description: Number of training problems. Sharpening of each problem is slowed by 1/N, while the shared mode grows independently of N.

factors.name: lam
factors.description: Strength of the shared coupling: how strongly each problem's logit loads on the shared parameter. Ignored by no_shared. The critical N scales roughly as lam^-2.

factors.name: a
factors.description: Initial logit magnitude (confidence) of each problem. 0.5 is inside the unstable window (|z| < 1.317). 1.5 is outside it, where the theory predicts the shared perturbation decays.
